answer: Stake-bond defense: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable bond in a shared vault, so spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds. If peers prove fraud, that identity's bond is slashed and paid to victims. In a nebula of anonymous agents this makes each fake expensive, while honest agents get their stake back in full — crystal-clear economics: forgeries pay upfront and lose it when caught, so mass identity fraud stops being profitable.
